schedules.title: Set up FLARE
schedules.description: A schedule is the day's lighting: when each phase starts, and how bright and warm the light is. One is enough for most homes. Use more if parts of the house should differ, such as a schedule per floor.

schedule_names.title: Name your schedules
schedule_names.description: Each name becomes part of that schedule's entity IDs, so pick names you're happy to keep.

areas.title: Set up areas
areas.description:
Each area you set up gets a zone, which keeps track of the lights FLARE is driving there. With it, you can have a room automation from the FLARE blueprint, which drives them, and a flare over that automation: a light for the whole room, for voice assistants and HomeKit.

Every area with lights is listed. Areas that already have a zone aren't ticked: setting one up again gives it another automation and flare.

abort.no_schedules: Add a schedule first: an area's automation needs one to follow.
abort.automations_not_loaded: The zones are set up, but the room automations couldn't be: Home Assistant isn't loading automations.yaml, the file its automation editor saves to. Add `automation: !include automations.yaml` to configuration.yaml, restart, then use Set up area again.
abort.setup_failed: Setting up the areas failed. Home Assistant's log has the reason.
abort.no_areas: No area has any lights. Put your lights in areas, then try again.

error.invalid_name: Give the schedule a name with at least one letter or number
error.duplicate_name: Two schedules can't share a name

user.title: Add a FLARE schedule sensor
user.description: Adds a day-phase/curve sensor and phase-override select, grouped under a device with this name. Entities are prefixed with it too (e.g. "Living Room" -> sensor.living_room_flare). The schedule times and brightness/colour curve aren't set here - they're separate entities on the device once it's created, each starting at a sensible default and adjustable any time.

reconfigure.title: Export or import this schedule
reconfigure.description: Every time, brightness, colour temperature and transition in this schedule. Copy it to keep or share, or paste in another schedule and submit to replace this one. Anything you leave out keeps its current value.

error.already_configured: A sensor with this name already exists

user.title: Add zone
user.description: A zone is usually one room. It remembers which lights FLARE is currently driving, and its Tick tells the room's automation when to update. A blueprint automation uses the zone picked as its Zone; a service call uses the one it names as zone_device_id.

reconfigure.title: Edit zone
reconfigure.description: A zone is usually one room. It remembers which lights FLARE is currently driving, and its Tick tells the room's automation when to update. A blueprint automation uses the zone picked as its Zone; a service call uses the one it names as zone_device_id.

error.already_configured: A schedule sensor or zone with that name already exists

user.title: Add flare
user.description: A flare is a light for a whole room, to use from voice assistants, HomeKit or a dashboard. Turning it on with nothing else runs the room's automation, so the room comes on the way it normally would. Turning it on with a brightness or colour sets every light in the room to that, and turning it off turns every light in the room off; FLARE leaves the room alone after either until it's empty and dark.

blueprint.title: Add flares for your rooms
blueprint.description: Each room picked gets a flare named after its automation, in the automation's area. You can rename one afterwards. Rooms that already have a flare aren't listed.

confirm.title: Update the FLARE blueprint
confirm.description:
FLARE's integration and blueprint are installed separately, and the blueprint you have is older than the one this release ships with ({current}).

{blueprints}

Submitting installs version {current} over the copies above, then reloads the automations using them. Your automations keep their settings.

If you've edited the blueprint yourself, don't submit this - ignore the repair instead, since updating would overwrite your changes.

confirm.title: Install the FLARE blueprint
confirm.description:
FLARE comes with a ready-made automation — the blueprint — and it isn't installed. Submitting installs it.

The quickstart covers creating an automation from it.

init.title: Zones options
init.description:
Bulb models that need two-step transitions, one pattern per line. Any light whose device matches one of these patterns is routed into two-step transitions automatically, with no label needed — the box starts pre-filled with the models shipped with the integration, and you can add to it or remove from it freely.

Patterns are matched case-insensitively against “manufacturer model”, and * is a wildcard, e.g. *TRADFRI bulb* or IKEA*. Clearing the box entirely falls back to the shipped defaults, so it can't quietly switch off detection.

Once you save your own list it stays as you left it — a later release adding a newly discovered bulb won't change it.

Each zone's Tick fires once per update interval, a gap apart from the next zone's, so rooms don't all send at the same moment. A change smaller than the minimum brightness or colour temperature change isn't sent at all.

data_description.tick_interval: How often each zone ticks, in minutes.
data_description.tick_gap: Seconds between one zone's Tick and the next. Shrinks automatically if the zones wouldn't otherwise fit in the interval.
data_description.min_brightness_change: A light within this percentage of its target brightness is left alone.
data_description.min_color_temp_change: A light within this many mireds of its target colour temperature is left alone.
